> "## Executive finding
>
> The object you want is most often **not indexed as “text + photo poster.”** In real search language it is usually called one of these:
>
> **“product key visual / product KV,” “campaign key visual,” “brand campaign still,” “product campaign art direction,” “promotional poster,” “poster system,” “launch visual,” “social static,” “OOH/static campaign,” “product poster,” “commercial still life + typography,”** or, in Chinese-language ecosystems, **产品KV / 品牌KV / 产品海报 / 商业海报 / 主视觉**.
>
> The highest-yield hunt is not broad inspiration platforms. It is a mix of **packaging/brand launch sites, type-in-use archives, advertising-print archives, commercial photography/still-life portfolios, and Asian KV/product-poster ecosystems**.
>
> ---
>
> # Primary hunt surfaces
>
> ## 1. **BP&O**
>
> **Why it fits:** BP&O is one of the strongest editorial surfaces for brand systems where product, packaging, photography, typography, posters, and social statics are shown together. It is not only packaging; many entries include **poster-like launch visuals, art-directed product photography, billboards, and typography systems**.
>
> **What appears there:**
> Object-led food, drink, coffee, beauty-adjacent, lifestyle product, alcohol, tech, music hardware, and packaging-led promos. The best BP&O entries often show the **brand world**: pack shots, posters, billboards, product stills, and type hierarchy in one system.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> Search result captions and article copy often name the exact asset classes: **posters, billboards, art direction, photography, wordmark, typography, packaging**. Recent examples include Yoshi by Saint-Urbain, where BP&O explicitly discusses packaging, posters, photography/art direction, billboard usage, and type choices in the same project. ([Richard Baird][1])
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:bpando.org product photography typography posters`
> * `site:bpando.org packaging posters photography art direction`
> * `site:bpando.org billboard product photography typography`
> * `site:bpando.org skincare packaging posters photography`
> * `site:bpando.org beverage branding posters typography photography`
>
> **Alignment score:** Very high. Best for **designed brand/product systems with poster statics** rather than one-off ads.
>
> ---
>
> ## 2. **The Brand Identity**
>
> **Why it fits:** The Brand Identity is strong for contemporary identity systems where the final visuals are often campaign-like: type, photography, product, social statics, packaging, and motion frames. It is especially useful from **2024–2026** because many entries are current studio launches.
>
> **What appears there:**
> Tech devices, beauty-adjacent products, food, lifestyle, skincare, home objects, hospitality products, and packaging-led brand systems. A 2026 example for Nothing’s Ear (3) is explicitly described as product photography with campaign materials and dot-matrix typography, sitting between product and beauty imagery. ([The Brand Identity][2])
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> The site’s project pages often include credits for **typography, campaign photography, packaging, advertising, posters, digital screens, and product photography**. It is good for spotting studios and photographers, then following those contributors directly.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:the-brandidentity.com "product photography" typography campaign`
> * `site:the-brandidentity.com packaging posters typography photography`
> * `site:the-brandidentity.com product campaign typography`
> * `site:the-brandidentity.com beauty product photography typography`
> * `site:the-brandidentity.com "campaign materials" typography product`
>
> **Alignment score:** High. Slightly more brand-system/editorial than pure ad archive, but very good for the exact “photo and type co-authored” logic.
>
> ---
>
> ## 3. **Fonts In Use**
>
> **Why it fits:** Fonts In Use is not a generic design gallery; it is a **searchable archive of typographic design indexed by typeface, format, and topic**. ([fontsinuse.com][3]) It has dedicated format/topic areas for **Advertising, Packaging, Object/Product, Posters/Flyers**, which lets you triangulate the object through type rather than through ad jargon. ([fontsinuse.com][4])
>
> **What appears there:**
> Packaging, advertising, posters, product identities, editorial-style launches, object/product type treatments. It is especially useful when the typography is not decorative but a major structural component.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> You can search by **format + industry + typeface**. For example, advertising has over a thousand Object/Product-related examples and packaging has thousands of entries. ([fontsinuse.com][4]) That makes it better than Pinterest when you need recoverable metadata: typeface, designer, studio, year, format.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:fontsinuse.com/uses product photography typography`
> * `site:fontsinuse.com/uses packaging advertising poster`
> * `site:fontsinuse.com/uses "product" "poster"`
> * `site:fontsinuse.com/uses "photography" "packaging"`
> * Use internal filters: **Advertising + Object/Product + Packaging + Posters/Flyers**
>
> **Alignment score:** Very high for typography-led hunting; medium for photography-led hunting. Best as a **metadata map**.
>
> ---
>
> ## 4. **World Brand Design Society / World Brand Design**
>
> **Why it fits:** World Brand Design is uneven, but high-yield for product categories: food, beverage, beauty, FMCG, packaging, alcohol, retail, and consumer goods. It repeatedly publishes projects where packaging extends into **poster-like visual systems**.
>
> **What appears there:**
> Packaging-led promos, product launch visuals, poster-inspired food/beverage identities, typographic packs, campaign extensions. Recent examples explicitly use language like **“street posters,” “sneaker campaign posters,” “trippy punk rock poster,” “poster-like statement,”** and **photography/product deliverables**. ([World Brand Design Society][5])
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> It is operational because posts are heavily tagged by **industry, format, deliverables, and substrate**. It is not always refined, but it surfaces a lot of smaller studios that do precisely the kind of object-led commercial visuals you are seeking.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:worldbranddesign.com product poster typography photography`
> * `site:worldbranddesign.com "poster-like" packaging`
> * `site:worldbranddesign.com "campaign posters" product`
> * `site:worldbranddesign.com "product photography" "typography"`
> * `site:worldbranddesign.com "sneaker campaign posters"`
>
> **Alignment score:** High yield, medium curation quality. Excellent for volume, but requires filtering.
>
> ---
>
> ## 5. **Dieline**
>
> **Why it fits:** Dieline is primarily packaging, but that is useful because many object-led commercial posters now come from **packaging systems extended into campaign statics**. Dieline describes itself as a leading source for packaging innovation and frequently covers beauty, health, beverage, food, home, and product packaging. ([DIELINE][6])
>
> **What appears there:**
> Packaging-led product visuals, food/beverage/product launches, beauty and health packaging, promotional packaging, product photography, brand collabs. It is especially useful when the pack itself is the hero object and typography becomes the spatial architecture.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> Dieline is not always poster-focused, but it is strong for finding the **source brands, agencies, packaging photographers, and full visual systems**. Their directory/category system includes agencies with capabilities like **product photography, packaging, print design, typography, and retail/environmental work**. ([DIELINE][7])
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:thedieline.com product photography typography packaging`
> * `site:thedieline.com beauty packaging product photography typography`
> * `site:thedieline.com beverage packaging posters typography`
> * `site:thedieline.com promotional packaging campaign photography`
> * `site:thedieline.com "loud typography" packaging`
>
> **Alignment score:** Medium-high. Best when the object is **packaging-led**; less reliable for standalone campaign statics.
>
> ---
>
> ## 6. **Ads of the World**
>
> **Why it fits:** Ads of the World is not a design-system site; it is an advertising archive. Its value is that you can filter for **Print** and **Static Images**, then search product categories. The site explicitly indexes creative ads by media type and industry, including print/static image categories. ([Ads of the World™][8])
>
> **What appears there:**
> Print ads, social statics, OOH, product ads, food/drink ads, beauty/health, household, retail. Some will be concept-led rather than type/photo-integrated, but it is one of the better surfaces for true commercial statics.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> It is good when you want **actual advertising output**, not just brand presentation mockups. Use it for “does this composition logic exist in deployed campaigns?” checks.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:adsoftheworld.com "Print" "Static Images" typography product`
> * `site:adsoftheworld.com "beauty" "typography" "print"`
> * `site:adsoftheworld.com "food" "typography" "static images"`
> * `site:adsoftheworld.com "product" "poster"`
> * internal filters: **Print / Static Images + Beauty / Food / Soft Drinks / Household / Electronics**
>
> **Alignment score:** High for true ads, medium for design refinement. Watch for clever-copy print ads where the object/type integration is weak.
>
> ---
>
> ## 7. **Lürzer’s Archive**
>
> **Why it fits:** Lürzer’s is a professional ad archive with decades of print, TV, digital, poster, and advertising work. It states that users can search 40 years of print campaigns, TV commercials, and digital designs, and its archive contains hand-picked ad campaigns across print, film, TV, and digital. ([Lurzers Archive][9])
>
> **What appears there:**
> High-level advertising print, posters, commercial photography, product ads, campaign stills, art-directed static ads.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> It is more curated than broad social platforms and more advertising-native than design blogs. A separate history piece describes Lürzer’s Archive as a magazine and worldwide database presenting advertisements, posters, TV commercials, digital and interactive advertising from around the world. ([АПА Фотографические искусства][10])
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * internal search: `product photography typography`
> * internal search: `print product poster`
> * internal search: `packaging typography`
> * internal search: `still life typography`
> * category filters: **Print / Posters / Product category / Photography**
>
> **Alignment score:** High for commercial relevance; access may be limited by subscription.
>
> ---
>
> ## 8. **ZCOOL / 站酷**
>
> **Why it fits:** For Asian commercial poster ecosystems, ZCOOL is one of the most directly aligned surfaces because Chinese commercial design uses the term **KV / 主视觉** very naturally. Search results show product KV, beauty product main visuals, product photography, commercial poster prompts, and service listings for **产品KV / 海报图摄影 / 视觉策划**. ([站酷 ZCOOL][11])
>
> **What appears there:**
> Beauty/skincare product KV, cosmetics, small appliances, drinks, food, e-commerce campaign posters, 3D/rendered product statics, product photography with type-safe negative space, Taobao/Tmall-style launch visuals.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> This is where the object is often named exactly as you need it: **产品KV海报, 品牌KV, 产品主视觉, 商业海报, 电商产品摄影, 美妆产品拍摄**. A 2026 ZCOOL result even describes a product KV promo poster with negative space reserved for big sans-serif sale typography. ([站酷 ZCOOL][12])
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:zcool.com.cn 产品KV 海报 摄影 字体`
> * `site:zcool.com.cn 美妆 产品KV 海报`
> * `site:zcool.com.cn 产品主视觉 摄影 字体`
> * `site:zcool.com.cn 商业海报 产品摄影 字体`
> * `site:zcool.com.cn 护肤品 产品海报 KV`
>
> **Alignment score:** Very high for Asian e-commerce/commercial product poster logic. Requires filtering out AI prompt sludge and template-like work.
>
> ---
>
> ## 9. **Huaban / 花瓣, BigBigWork, Chinese visual-reference aggregators**
>
> **Why it fits:** These are closer to reference-board ecosystems than editorial sources, but they preserve the language and category structure used by Chinese commercial designers: **产品KV, 品牌KV, 主视觉, 商业海报, 产品海报**. BigBigWork search snippets show product KV and brand KV results; Huaban boards group “产品KV,” “品牌,” “摄影,” and “字体” as practical commercial reference categories. ([Большие Работы][13])
>
> **What appears there:**
> Beauty, drinks, FMCG, e-commerce campaign visuals, product launch posters, 3D object scenes, retail festival promo statics.
>
> **Why useful for repeated hunting:**
> Good for **vocabulary discovery and pattern recognition**, less good for final sourcing. Use them to identify Chinese terms, studios, and composition tropes, then reverse-search or follow the studio to ZCOOL, Behance, Xiaohongshu, WeChat, or agency portfolios.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `产品KV 字体 摄影`
> * `品牌KV 产品摄影`
> * `商业海报 产品摄影 字体设计`
> * `主视觉 产品 海报`
> * `美妆 KV 海报 字体`
>
> **Alignment score:** High as a hunting index; medium-low as a citation/final-source surface.
>
> ---
>
> # Adjacent support surfaces
>
> ## 10. **Commercial still-life photographers and retouchers’ portfolios**
>
> **Why it fits:** Many of the best examples never appear on design blogs because they live on the portfolios of photographers, retouchers, CGI artists, or art directors. Search by **“still life advertising,” “product photographer campaign,” “beauty still life,” “commercial still life typography,” “retouching campaign stills.”**
>
> **What appears there:**
> Perfume, skincare, beauty, drinks, watches, jewelry, sneakers, tech, home objects. Often object-led and compositionally sophisticated.
>
> **How to hunt:**
>
> * `commercial still life product campaign typography`
> * `beauty still life campaign typography`
> * `fragrance still life poster typography`
> * `product photographer campaign key visual`
> * `retouching product campaign poster`
>
> **Use as:** High-quality source discovery after you identify a brand/studio from BP&O, The Brand Identity, Dieline, or Ads of the World.
>
> ---
>
> ## 11. **Agency portfolio pages**
>
> **Why it fits:** The best static systems are often shown in the agency’s own case page with full campaign grids: product stills, social statics, posters, billboards, e-comm banners, packaging, and motion frames.
>
> **What appears there:**
> Much stronger context than gallery reposts. You can see whether the type/photo integration is systemic or just one lucky frame.
>
> **How to hunt:**
>
> * `site:studio-name.com product campaign typography photography`
> * `site:agency.com key visual product campaign`
> * `site:agency.com product launch posters`
> * `site:agency.com beauty campaign art direction typography`
> * `site:agency.com packaging campaign photography posters`
>
> **Use as:** Verification surface. Once a gallery shows one frame, find the agency page to get the full static set.
>
> ---
>

> Search by **studio, photographer, retoucher, brand, or exact KV terms**, not by generic “poster design.”

> ## 13. **Japanese design institutions and annuals: JAGDA / Tokyo ADC / JPDA**
>
> **Why it fits:** Japan has a strong poster and commercial graphic design culture, but many institutional surfaces are more award/exhibition-oriented than product-search-friendly. JAGDA’s 2025 exhibition page confirms its role in gathering current Japanese graphic design work across region and discipline. ([公益社団法人日本グラフィックデザイン協会（JAGDA）][14])
>
> **What appears there:**
> More posters, cultural graphics, identity, packaging, and campaign systems than e-commerce product KVs. Object-led commercial examples exist but are less directly searchable.
>
> **Use queries like:**
>
> * `site:jagda.or.jp product poster typography`
> * `site:tokyoadc.com product advertising poster`
> * `商品 ポスター タイポグラフィ 写真 広告`

> * `キービジュアル 商品 広告 タイポグラフィ`
>
> **Alignment score:** Medium. Strong design quality; less efficient for object-led commercial statics unless you know designers/agencies.

>
> **Why it fits:** Korea has strong beauty, skincare, food, and consumer-product static ecosystems, but the searchable public surfaces are fragmented: agency sites, Naver blogs, design magazines, Instagram, Behance, and brand campaign pages.
>
> **Use vocabulary:**
>

>
> **Best categories:**
> Beauty, skincare, cosmetics, drinks, food, tech accessories, pop-up retail.

> **Alignment score:** High visually, medium operationally. Best reached through Korean brands, agencies, and photographer portfolios rather than general galleries.

> # Naming: what this object is probably called
>
> ## Most likely real-world labels
>
> Use these labels because they match how agencies, designers, and Asian commercial teams actually publish the work:
>
> 1. **Product key visual / product KV**
>    Best overall label. Especially strong in Asian commercial design and e-commerce contexts.
>
> 2. **Campaign key visual**
>    Broader than product KV; useful for brand launches, product launches, and OOH/social static systems.
>
> 3. **Product campaign still / campaign static**
>    Useful in advertising and production contexts.
>
> 4. **Product poster / promotional poster**
>    Useful but broader. Works well when combined with typography/photography/object terms.
>
> 5. **Commercial still life with typography**
>    Useful for photography/retouching/CGI portfolios.
>
> 6. **Packaging campaign / packaging-led campaign visual**
>    Best when the physical pack is the hero object.
>
> 7. **Poster system / campaign poster system**
>    Useful for identity projects where the poster logic repeats across many statics.
>
> 8. **Brand world stills / brand campaign stills**
>    Good for newer studio language, especially 2024–2026 brand-system projects.
>
> ---
>
> ## Labels that are too broad or misleading
>
> Avoid these as primary search terms:
>
> * **text over image** — too generic and usually low quality.
> * **graphic design poster** — returns cultural posters, student work, music, events.
> * **typography poster** — mostly type-only, experimental, event, or student work.
> * **product photography** — too broad; gives packshots without type integration.
> * **branding case study** — too broad; often mockups, logo systems, strategy slides.
> * **advertising campaign** — too broad; video, activation, PR, case-film results.
> * **print ad** — useful only with filters; otherwise concept ads, social issues, awards work.
> * **poster design inspiration** — sludge magnet.
> * **packaging design** — useful only if paired with campaign/poster/photography terms.
> * **social media design** — usually templates and marketplace creatives.
> * **key art** — often entertainment, gaming, film, not product statics.
> * **hero image** — too web/e-commerce oriented unless paired with product typography.
>
> ---
>
> # Surfaces to avoid by default
>
> ## Avoid unless you are deliberately doing loose visual moodboarding
>
> * **Pinterest** — good for visual trails, bad for provenance and recency.
> * **Dribbble** — too much UI, speculative design, template-style work.
> * **Behance broad search** — can be useful only with precise regional terms like `产品KV`, but broad Behance search is noisy.
> * **Freepik / Shutterstock / Vecteezy / stock sites** — mostly templates, mockups, generic assets.
> * **Canva template libraries** — not aligned with authored photo/type composition.
> * **Movie-poster databases** — wrong object class.
> * **Museum poster archives** — historically rich but not current commercial product statics.
> * **Generic packaging blogs** — use only if they show campaign extensions, not just pack renders.
> * **UI/UX galleries** — wrong medium.
> * **Marketplace creative galleries** — too template-driven.
> * **AI prompt galleries** — useful only for vocabulary drift, not for source-quality references.
>
> ---
>
> # Best operational search stack
>
> Use this order:
>
> 1. **BP&O / The Brand Identity**
>    Find refined brand/product systems with posters, photography, and type.
>
> 2. **Fonts In Use**
>    Backdoor through typography metadata: Advertising + Packaging + Object/Product + Posters.
>
> 3. **World Brand Design / Dieline**
>    Expand into packaging-led product systems and smaller studios.
>
> 4. **Ads of the World / Lürzer’s Archive**
>    Validate true deployed commercial/static advertising.
>
> 5. **ZCOOL / Chinese KV searches**
>    Hunt Asian product-poster and e-commerce KV ecosystems with the correct vocabulary.
>
> 6. **Agency, photographer, retoucher, CGI artist portfolios**
>    Find the strongest complete sets and production credits.
>
> 7. **Instagram / Xiaohongshu / WeChat / Naver / Behance**
>    Use only with precise terms and names gathered from the above.
>
> ---

> # Practical shortlist
>
> The strongest repeatable surfaces are:
>
> 8. **BP&O** — best refined brand/product systems with posters and product photography.
> 9. **The Brand Identity** — best current studio-led campaign/identity visuals, 2025–2026 especially.
> 10. **Fonts In Use** — best typography-first archive; excellent for finding object/product and advertising cases.
> 11. **World Brand Design** — high-volume product/packaging campaign source; filter hard.
> 12. **Dieline** — best for packaging-led product promos and product categories.
> 13. **Ads of the World** — best for deployed print/static commercial ads.
> 14. **Lürzer’s Archive** — best professional advertising archive, especially print/poster/commercial photography.
> 15. **ZCOOL / 站酷** — best Asian product KV and beauty/e-commerce poster ecosystem.
> 16. **Huaban / BigBigWork / Xiaohongshu-style Chinese searches** — best vocabulary and pattern discovery, weaker provenance.
> 17. **Photographer/retoucher/agency portfolios** — best final-quality source once names are discovered.

Да, здесь уже видно главный failure mode: не просто “не те сайты”, а **невалидированные термины**.
То есть следующий проход должен запрещать две вещи:

- нельзя рекомендовать surface, если предложенные запросы там не дают релевантных попаданий;
- нельзя рекомендовать term/tag, если он не бьётся хотя бы на нескольких живых surfaces.

`World Brand Design` и `The Dieline` я уже добавил в approved layer и дашборд как **полезные соседние surfaces**, но не как доказанные exact-match hits.

Я бы теперь split сделал так, чтобы это снова не слиплось.

**1. Deep Research: validated naming + tag bank**
```text
Conduct a research study to determine the real search language for poster-like commercial statics in which typography and photography are compositionally integrated.

Calibration:
Use these examples only as directional calibration, not as a rigid style template:
- object/product-led promotional statics
- poster-like frames
- type and image co-authored as one composition
- oversized type, type behind object, type as backdrop, type interacting with crop/perspective/negative space
- preferably physical products: drinks, skincare, beauty, sneakers, chairs, packaging, devices, food, household goods

Goal:
I do not want generic design terms. I want only search language that actually retrieves this object in practice.

Critical validation rule:
Do not recommend any term, tag, phrase, or hashtag unless it has been tested against real search surfaces and shown to retrieve matching examples. If a term sounds plausible but does not produce relevant results, reject it.

What to return:
1. A validated naming stack:
   - core terms
   - adjacent useful terms
   - multilingual terms if they materially improve recall
2. For each term:
   - what it tends to retrieve
   - whether it is precise, adjacent, or drift-prone
   - which surfaces it actually worked on
3. A reject list of misleading terms that sound right but fail in practice.
4. Tight query recipes for Google/web search and for platform-specific search.

Requirements:
- prioritize 2024–2026 usage
- include Asian commercial ecosystems if they materially improve retrieval
- do not pad the vocabulary
- if a term fails validation, drop it
```

**2. Manual web search: surfaces that actually contain this object**
```text
Run a manual web-search pass to find repeatable surfaces where poster-like commercial statics with integrated typography + product/object photography actually appear.

Target object:
Not generic branding, not generic packaging, not generic campaign case studies, not generic “text over image.” I want poster-like promotional frames where text and image are compositionally dependent.

Critical rule:
A surface can only be kept if the proposed search behavior on that surface produces multiple relevant examples of this exact object class. If the surface is nice in general but the object does not actually surface there, reject it.

What to return:
1. A kept list of surfaces / sites / platforms / source classes.
2. For each one:
   - what kind of matching work appears there
   - whether it is primary or adjacent
   - what exact search behavior works there
   - what failed there
3. Separate:
   - primary hunt surfaces
   - adjacent support surfaces
   - surfaces that looked promising but failed validation
4. Explain why each kept surface survived.

Exclude:
- marketplace creatives
- UI/UX galleries
- movie-poster / museum-poster archives
- generic branding sites where the target object does not actually surface
- surfaces where recommended keywords do not hit relevant results

Requirements:
- fewer stronger surfaces over completeness
- no case lists as the main deliverable
- every kept surface must be operationally testable
```

**3. Deep Research: studios / agencies / photographers / accounts**
```text
Conduct a research study to find who repeatedly produces poster-like commercial statics where typography and product/object photography are integrated into one composed frame.

Goal:
I want makers and publishing surfaces, not one-off campaign examples. This can include agencies, design studios, photographers, retouchers, CGI artists, production studios, Instagram accounts, Xiaohongshu / Chinese visual accounts, or other repeatable publisher surfaces.

Calibration:
The object is object-led promotional imagery with strong type-image integration, not just generic ad campaigns and not pure packaging.

Critical validation rule:
Do not keep a studio, account, or publisher unless there is repeated evidence that they produce or publish this exact object class. One lucky frame is not enough.

What to return:
1. A kept list of:
   - studios / agencies
   - photographers / image-makers
   - accounts / publishing pages
2. For each:
   - what object categories they are strongest in
   - whether they are product-led, poster-like, or packaging-led
   - where they publish
   - whether they are luxury-skewed, middle-market, or mass-commercial
3. Separate:
   - direct makers
   - repeatable publishing accounts
   - adjacent but weaker leads
4. Include search paths for finding more from each source.

Requirements:
- prioritize 2024–2026
- include Asian ecosystems where relevant
- do not return generic famous studios unless their output really matches this object
- no one-off case pages as the main answer
```

- чтобы `термин реально работал` на surface;

- чтобы результат не скатывался в `колхозный 2015 local promo`, даже если формально это `product + type`.

>
> ## 4. Tight query recipes
>
> ### Google / web search
>
> Use **product category + core term + typography/composition modifier**.
>
> Best general recipes:
>
> * `"product poster design" typography skincare`
> * `"product poster design" "bold typography" beverage`
> * `"product key visual" skincare typography`
> * `"advertising key visual" product typography`
> * `"product ad poster" "bold typography"`
> * `"product manipulation poster" beverage typography`
> * `"social media product post design" "bold typography"`
> * `"product poster design" sneaker "type"`
> * `"product poster design" cosmetics "typography"`
> * `"commercial poster design" product typography "Behance"`
>
> For the exact object you described, the strongest combined query is:
>
> **`"product poster design" "bold typography" product photography`**
>
> For higher-end agency/campaign references:
>
> **`"product key visual" "product photography" typography`**
>
> For Photoshop/composite-style statics:
>
> **`"product manipulation poster" "typography"`**
>

> ## Final naming recommendation
>
> Use this stack in order:
>
> 1. **product poster design** — best everyday search term.
> 2. **product key visual** — best agency/commercial campaign term.

> 4. **product ad poster** — useful, but more tutorial/template-heavy.

**Final prompt**
```text
Conduct a deep research study to find direct resources for a very specific visual object:

poster-like commercial statics where typography and photography are compositionally integrated into one frame, preferably around a physical product or object.

Calibration:
I do NOT want generic “text over image,” generic branding, generic packaging, generic campaign case studies, or dated cheap promo graphics. I want current, stylish, trend-forward 2025–2026 work where the text feels structurally fused with the image: oversized type, type behind object, type as backdrop, type interacting with crop/perspective/negative space, or otherwise co-authored with the photo.

Preferred object categories:
skincare, beauty, fragrance, drinks, food, sneakers, watches, furniture, home objects, packaging-led promos, tech devices, consumer goods.

What I need:
not case lists.
I need:
1. validated search vocabulary,
2. direct resources,
3. direct studios / agencies / photographers / accounts / publisher nodes,
where this exact object can actually be found.

Critical validation rules:
- Do not recommend a term unless it was tested and actually retrieves matching work.
- Do not recommend a site unless the object really appears there repeatedly.
- Do not give generic platform search pages (Behance, Dribbble, Pinterest, Instagram search, etc.) as final resources.
- If a result is stylistically dated, cheap, template-like, 2015-looking, or e-commerce-collage-like, reject it even if it formally matches the object.
- Prefer fewer strong resources over padded completeness.

What to return:
1. Exact naming:
   - what this object is most likely called in real search language.
2. Validated tag/query bank:
   - core terms,
   - adjacent useful terms,
   - Chinese / Japanese / Korean terms if they materially improve recall,
   - reject terms that sounded plausible but failed.
3. Direct resources:
   - sites/surfaces where this object repeatedly appears.
4. Direct makers/publisher nodes:
   - studios, agencies, photographers, retouchers, creative accounts, publisher pages that repeatedly produce or publish this object.
5. Separate results into:
   - primary hunt resources,
   - adjacent useful resources,
   - reject / misleading resources.

Priority:
current 2025–2026 style quality over sheer volume.
Asian commercial poster/KV ecosystems are welcome if they are genuinely strong and current.
```

**Prompt notes**
- Режим: `Deep Research`
- Главная защита: `не кейсы`, `не generic platforms as answer`, `не колхозный 2015`
- Выход: `validated tags + direct resources + direct studios/accounts`

Если хочешь самый безопасный вариант на 3 ночи, используй именно этот, ничего не меняя.

> "## 1. Exact naming: what this object is most likely called
>
> The strongest real-world name is **product key visual** / **product-led key visual**, usually shortened to **KV** in Asian commercial-design ecosystems. In Western studio/publisher language, the same object is more often described as **campaign imagery**, **campaign assets**, **launch campaign**, **brand world**, **product photography**, **still-life campaign**, or **social assets** rather than “poster.”
>
> For your very specific target, the most useful compound is:
>
> **product-led key visual + typography-led campaign imagery**
>
> That phrase captures the object better than “poster design,” because current work is usually delivered as stills for launch pages, paid social, OOH, carousels, campaign systems, and digital ads, not just posters. “Key visual” also tested especially well for product categories: World Brand Design Society uses “product-led key visual templates” in an RTD drink relaunch, and a 2025 Mizo Prote!n campaign is indexed around packaging, campaign, product photography, and spring 2025 launch language. ([World Brand Design Society][1])
>
> ## 2. Validated tag / query bank
>
> ### Core terms that actually retrieved matching work
>
> Use these as exact search strings:
>
> * **“product key visual” typography photography**
> * **“product-led key visual” campaign**
> * **“campaign imagery” “product photography” typography**
> * **“product photography” “oversized typography” campaign**
> * **“still life” product campaign typography**
> * **“brand world” product photography campaign**
> * **“launch campaign” skincare typography product photography**
> * **“social assets” product photography typography**
> * **“product photography” “art direction” “campaign” skincare**
> * **“product photography” “typography” “food/beverage” campaign**
>
> Best calibration evidence: The Brand Identity’s 2026 Nothing Ear (3) article explicitly frames product imagery as between **product photography** and beauty territory, with dot-matrix typography across campaign materials; its Jewel article uses **grid-based typography** plus **precise product photography**; and its Night & Day drinks project describes label layout behaving like a bold, graphic screen-print rather than a normal label. ([The Brand Identity][2])
>
> ### Adjacent useful terms
>
> These do not always hit the exact object, but they improve recall when combined with product categories:
>
> * **campaign assets**
> * **brand universe**
> * **brand world**
> * **go-to-market campaign**
> * **launch-ready key visual templates**
> * **product-led campaign**
> * **still-life art direction**
> * **editorial product photography**
> * **typography-led identity**
> * **social campaign system**
> * **OOH key visual**
> * **packaging-led campaign**
> * **macro product imagery**
> * **full-bleed product imagery**
> * **oversized typography**
> * **layered typography**
> * **bento-grid layout system**
>
> “Brand world” and “campaign assets” are especially good when hunting studio portfolios, because many 2025–2026 brand projects present the same visual object as a system rather than as a single poster. The Phoney Club, for example, describes CÎME-related output in terms of brand campaigns, product photography, seasonal campaigns, digital ads, editorial, and social imagery. ([THE PHONEY CLUB][3])
>
> ### Chinese / Japanese / Korean terms that materially improve recall
>
> **Chinese**
>
> * **产品主视觉**
> * **产品 KV**
> * **主视觉海报**
> * **美妆 主视觉**

>
> These retrieve a lot of template trash, but **产品主视觉 + 字体 + 美妆 / 香水 / 饮品** is still useful for Chinese-speaking commercial/KV ecosystems. Search results showed many “产品主视觉” and “kv主视觉” pages, but much of it was PSD/template-led, so use these only as discovery inputs, not as quality filters. ([youngem.com][4])

> ### Reject terms that sounded plausible but failed quality control
>
> * **“text over image”** — too generic; retrieves tutorials, Canva-style layouts, basic ads.
> * **“product poster design”** — too template-heavy and often dated.
> * **“commercial poster design advertising”** — too broad; lots of cheap promo graphics.
> * **“product advertisement poster”** — strongly polluted by low-end social ads.
> * **“ecommerce product photography background”** — retrieves marketplace/photo-background advice, not integrated type/photo composition.
> * **“key visual stock”** — stock vectors and generic layouts, not art-directed commercial statics.
> * **“banner design product”** — mostly templates and e-commerce collateral.
> * **“social media product post design”** — over-indexes cheap Instagram carousel templates.
> * **“packaging design typography”** alone — useful category, but not enough; retrieves packaging case studies without fused typography/photo statics.

> **Dragon Rouge Singapore** — validated for Odd Company RTD: explicitly built “launch-ready key visual templates” that were both product-led and talent-led. Good node for Asia-Pacific FMCG/drinks. ([World Brand Design Society][1])
>
> **BolkoDesign** — validated for Mizo Prote!n: 2025 food/beverage product line, packaging, go-to-market campaign, product photography, and campaign deliverables. ([World Brand Design Society][8])
>
> **Uncommon** — relevant when the object becomes type/layout-heavy beauty advertising. The Ordinary campaign is not product-object-forward enough for your core target, but it validates the current beauty-advertising language of stark imagery, type, layout, and white space. ([It's Nice That][13])
>
> **Margarita van Werven** — strong beauty/cosmetics still-life node; validated by 2026 Clinique work and third-party trend coverage noting still-life work for Oribe, Guerlain, and Ouai. Best as a photography/source node rather than a typography-layout node. ([Инстаграм][14])
>
> ### Publisher / curator nodes
>
> **The Brand Identity** — primary publisher node for taste-filtered current brand/campaign systems.
>
> **It’s Nice That** — trend-forward editorial validation; best for 2025–2026 design language and named makers.
>
> **World Brand Design Society** — high-yield but requires strict filtering; good for packaging-led promos, FMCG, drinks, beauty, and Asian/global agencies.
>
> **Mindsparkle Mag** — useful for brand identity + packaging + product imagery systems; apply currentness filter.
>
> **BP&O** — useful for refined packaging/identity systems; tested results showed 2025 examples in beauty/skincare and drinks, but it is more review/identity-oriented than campaign-static-specific. ([Richard Baird][15])
>
> ## 5. Adjacent useful resources
>
> These are worth mining, but not as primary sources:
>
> **Instagram account pages of studios/photographers** — often where the exact stills live first. Use only named accounts found through direct publisher pages or studio credits, not generic Instagram search. Examples surfaced: Little Troop, The Phoney Club, MOUTHWASH, Margarita van Werven. ([It's Nice That][7])
>
> **Agency service pages for “content cycle” / “brand universe” / “product photography”** — useful because this work is often sold as always-on assets rather than posters. The Phoney Club page is the best validated example. ([THE PHONEY CLUB][3])
>
> **Asian KV vocabulary searches** — useful for discovery, especially Chinese **产品主视觉 / 产品 KV / 美妆 主视觉**, but heavily polluted by templates and PSD marketplaces. Use as a lead generator only. ([youngem.com][4])
>
> ## 6. Reject / misleading resources
>
> **Pinterest boards and Pinterest idea pages** — visually rich, but too many dead ends, reposts, undated images, AI slop, and uncredited work. Useful for mood detection, not final sourcing.
>
> **Behance generic search pages** — too much student/concept work, duplicated mockups, weak case-study padding, and dated “social media ad” aesthetics. Individual Behance projects can be useful only when discovered via a credited maker.
>
> **Shutterstock / stock “key visual” pages** — rejected. The tested results returned generic stock vectors, sports logos, e-commerce backgrounds, and template-like layouts rather than stylish fused product/type photography. ([Шаттерсток][16])
>
> **Template marketplaces / PSD素材 / 58pic / Pikbest / Canva-style results** — rejected for final resources. They retrieve “formal matches” but fail the style-quality test: cheap, template-led, e-commerce-collage-like, or visually dated. ([58pic][17])
>
> **Generic “product photography background” blogs** — rejected for the core task. They discuss backdrops and e-commerce product-photo optimization, not structural fusion of type and image. ([Omi][18])
>
> ## Practical hunting recipe
>
> Start with:
>
> **“product-led key visual” “typography”**
> then branch into:
>
> **site:the-brandidentity.com product photography typography campaign**
> **site:worldbranddesign.com “key visual” “product photography” “typography”**
> **site:itsnicethat.com skincare typography campaign product photography**
> **site:mindsparklemag.com oversized typography product photography**
>
> For Asia/KV recall, use:
>
> **产品主视觉 字体 美妆**
> **产品 KV 摄影 海报**
> **商品キービジュアル 撮影 化粧品**
> **제품 키비주얼 화장품 타이포그래피**
>
> Then filter manually for the thing you actually want: **type participating in the photograph’s spatial logic**, not simply text placed on top after the fact.

> я хотела табличку со ссылками на ресурс и чтобы там было минимум несколько работ под мой запрос
> как Fonts In Use ты мне дал полезный для типографических приемов и текстовых
>
> Пока что получается так, что самый продуктивный способ — это искать в Pinterest по похожим, ну вот. Это меня устраивает плохо, потому что Pinterest много мусора выводит. Мне хочется, чтобы ты мне дал действительно качественные такие постеры или что это, в общем, связку продуктов, продукта с текстом. И чтобы это было современно и качественно. Понимаешь? И я не верю, что нет ни одного места, где бы лежало их много, ну либо хотя бы несколько. Может быть, внутри кейсов, может быть, внутри просто как источники вдохновения.

Понял точнее: тебе нужен не список тегов сам по себе и не россыпь кейсов, а **таблица ресурсов**, где каждый ресурс выживает только если внутри него реально есть **минимум несколько** современных, качественных, poster-like работ под твой объект.
Я заложу жёсткое допущение: `ресурс держим только если в нём найдено >= 3 прямых совпадения`.

**Final prompt**
```text
Conduct a deep research study to find real resource surfaces where this exact visual object repeatedly appears:

poster-like commercial statics in which typography and product/object photography are compositionally fused into one frame.

Target object:
Not generic text-over-image, not generic branding, not generic packaging, not generic case studies. I want modern, stylish, quality commercial visuals where text behaves as part of the image architecture: oversized type, type behind the object, type acting as backdrop, type interacting with crop/perspective/negative space, or otherwise structurally integrated with the photo.

Preferred object classes:
skincare, beauty, fragrance, drinks, food, sneakers, watches, furniture, home objects, tech devices, packaging-led promos, consumer goods.

Quality bar:
Prioritize 2025–2026 visual language. Reject dated, cheap, template-like, 2015-looking promo graphics, low-end e-commerce collage aesthetics, generic social-media ad templates, and noisy “design inspiration” sludge.

What I want back:
a table of resources, not a tag dump and not a case list.

Critical survival rule for every resource:
Keep a resource only if it contains at least 3 clearly matching works for this exact object class.
If it has only 1 lucky example, reject it.
If it is a broad platform (Pinterest, Behance, Dribbble, Instagram search, etc.), do not keep it as a final resource unless you can point to a very specific sub-surface, account, board, studio page, or repeatable node that consistently contains matching work.

What to return:
1. A kept table of the best resources.
2. For each resource, include:
   - resource name
   - direct link
   - what kind of matching work appears there
   - why it qualifies
   - minimum 3 direct example links from inside that resource
   - whether it skews beauty/skincare, food/drink, fashion-product, furniture/home, tech, or mixed
   - whether it is primary or adjacent
   - limitations
3. A reject table:
   - resources that looked promising but failed because the examples were too few, too dated, too generic, or too low-quality
4. A short validated vocabulary layer:
   - only the search terms that actually helped uncover the kept resources
   - reject misleading terms that produced cheap or off-brief work

Important:
Do not satisfy this request with generic “go search Behance / Pinterest / Dribbble.”
Do not return named campaigns as the main output.
Use Pinterest only as a lead source if needed, not as a final authority.
If the field is fragmented, prefer a smaller but trustworthy table over fake completeness.
```

**Prompt notes**
- Output object: `resource table with proof`
- Hard gate: `>= 3 matching works per resource`
- Style gate: `must feel current and professional, not template-like`
- Pinterest/Behance/Dribbble: `not final answers unless narrowed to a repeatable node`

> расскажи пока что свои догадки почему на пинтерест таких работ полно а напрямую сайты с ними мы найти не можем?

Мои текущие гипотезы такие.

1. Pinterest показывает не `источник`, а `след`. Он отлично собирает визуально похожие картинки, даже если у них плохая атрибуция, мёртвая ссылка, кроп, репост или вообще вырванный кусок из чужого кейса.

2. У этого объекта, похоже, нет одного нормального имени. Одни и те же штуки могут называться `KV`, `main visual`, `product poster`, `launch visual`, `campaign asset`, `social static`, `e-commerce poster`, `brand imagery`. Когда имя плавает, нормальный поиск ломается, а Pinterest всё равно находит по картинке.

3. Очень вероятно, что большая часть таких работ живёт в `закрытых или полу-закрытых экосистемах`: Instagram, Xiaohongshu, WeChat, ZCOOL, agency posts, временные launch pages, brand socials. Они плохо индексируются обычным вебом, но хорошо просачиваются в Pinterest.

4. Многие такие картинки, возможно, вообще не лежат в “архивах рекламы”. Они лежат:
- у студии в одном проекте
- у фотографа в портфолио
- у ретушёра
- в посте бренда
- в e-commerce / launch ecosystem
То есть источник фрагментирован.

5. Pinterest может смешивать три разных класса, которые внешне похожи:
- реальные кампейн-статики
- дизайнерские KV-постеры для портфолио
- полу-коммерческие e-commerce / promo visuals
Глазом они похожи, а источник у них разный.

6. Поисковики и сайты требуют `слов`, а Pinterest работает через `визуальную близость`. Для такого объекта это огромная разница. Если мы не попали в точное naming, обычный поиск отдаёт мусор, а Pinterest всё равно вытаскивает похожее.

7. Есть ещё региональный слой. Судя по твоим примерам, часть сильного материала может быть из китайского / вьетнамского / корейского commercial ecosystem, где naming, платформы и привычки публикации другие. Для Google это периферия, для Pinterest это просто “красивые картинки”.

То есть моя главная догадка такая:
**Pinterest создаёт иллюзию, что существует один большой архив этих работ, а на самом деле это рассыпанные фрагменты из разных экосистем, плохо именованные и плохо индексируемые.**

Из этого следует полезный вывод:
искать надо не `один сайт с большим архивом`, а, скорее всего, `2–4 типа источников`, где этот объект периодически всплывает:
- regional KV ecosystems
- studio / photographer / retoucher portfolios
- brand launch / social / promo pages
- curated repost surfaces с хорошей атрибуцией

Если хочешь, следующим сообщением я помогу тебе сформулировать именно **эту гипотезу как исследовательский prompt**: не “найди картинки”, а “почему Pinterest их знает, а веб не знает, и где тогда их настоящий source layer”.

> ## Validated vocabulary layer
>
> These terms actually helped uncover the kept resources:
>
> | Helpful search term                                         | Why it worked                                                                                             |
> | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | **“product photography typography campaign”**               | Best general phrase for finding cases where type and product imagery are discussed together.              |
> | **“packaging campaign photography typography”**             | Better than “poster design” because modern CPG work is often filed under packaging/campaign, not posters. |
> | **“product photography art direction typography”**          | Helped surface editorial reviews that discuss the image system, not just the logo.                        |
> | **“skincare typography photography campaign”**              | Useful for beauty/skincare-specific cases, but needed filtering.                                          |
> | **“brand identity packaging product photography campaign”** | Good for studio work archives where the output is a full commercial visual system.                        |
> | **Studio-name + “product photography typography campaign”** | Best precision move once a promising studio surfaced: Wedge, CENTER, Gander, Saint-Urbain, etc.           |
>
> Misleading terms I would avoid:
>
> | Misleading term                   | Why it failed                                                                      |
> | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | **“skincare poster design”**      | Overproduces Canva-like templates, Pinterest reposts, and cheap social ad layouts. |
> | **“beauty ad template”**          | Mostly stock, AI, and generic e-commerce collage aesthetics.                       |
> | **“text over product image”**     | Too generic; catches basic ad overlays rather than structural type/photo fusion.   |
> | **“luxury product shoot”**        | Good photography, but often no integrated typography.                              |
> | **“product ad design Photoshop”** | Tutorial/template-heavy and visually dated.                                        |
> | **“social media product banner”** | Skews low-end performance-ad layouts rather than modern art-directed statics.      |

> ## Validated vocabulary layer
>
> These terms actually helped uncover the kept resources:
>
> | Helpful search term                                         | Why it worked                                                                                             |
> | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | **“product photography typography campaign”**               | Best general phrase for finding cases where type and product imagery are discussed together.              |
> | **“packaging campaign photography typography”**             | Better than “poster design” because modern CPG work is often filed under packaging/campaign, not posters. |
> | **“product photography art direction typography”**          | Helped surface editorial reviews that discuss the image system, not just the logo.                        |
> | **“skincare typography photography campaign”**              | Useful for beauty/skincare-specific cases, but needed filtering.                                          |
> | **“brand identity packaging product photography campaign”** | Good for studio work archives where the output is a full commercial visual system.                        |
> | **Studio-name + “product photography typography campaign”** | Best precision move once a promising studio surfaced: Wedge, CENTER, Gander, Saint-Urbain, etc.           |
>
> Misleading terms I would avoid:
>
> | Misleading term                   | Why it failed                                                                      |
> | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | **“skincare poster design”**      | Overproduces Canva-like templates, Pinterest reposts, and cheap social ad layouts. |
> | **“beauty ad template”**          | Mostly stock, AI, and generic e-commerce collage aesthetics.                       |
> | **“text over product image”**     | Too generic; catches basic ad overlays rather than structural type/photo fusion.   |
> | **“luxury product shoot”**        | Good photography, but often no integrated typography.                              |
> | **“product ad design Photoshop”** | Tutorial/template-heavy and visually dated.                                        |
> | **“social media product banner”** | Skews low-end performance-ad layouts rather than modern art-directed statics.      |

1. Для этой ветки мы полностью **отключаем white list** как источник рекомендаций, пока там нет ни одного прямого попадания под твой запрос?

2. Правильно ли я понимаю твой критерий `target-resource` так:
   сайт или конкретный раздел сайта, где **без прыжков по кейсам** видно хотя бы `3–5` современных, стильных, on-brief работ с `product/object + integrated type`?

3. Если таких ресурсов окажется очень мало, ты хочешь следующий заход сформулировать уже не как `дай список ресурсов`, а как:
   `найди первый настоящий target-surface, если он вообще существует, и не подменяй его соседними студийными архивами`?

> Тебе не отключаем мы его или нет? Тут просто есть хотя бы примерные намёки на то, что я считаю стильным, какие источники я считаю стильными. А если этой опоры не будет, не знаю, смотри сам.
>
> Второй вопрос. Да, просто ты мне ни одного не дал. Вообще ни за всё время ни разу ни одного. Их не может оказаться мало. Я тебе дам подсказку: под мой критерий подходят даже карточки для Marketplace. Например, мы гуглим: «качественные карточки для Marketplace», и тебе действительно может высветиться хороший классный работ с красиво интегрированным текстом. И в Инстаграме это тоже может встретиться.
>
> Понимаешь, ты просто как-то не так ищешь, я убеждена. Это не обязательно даже... Я не знаю, в чём стопор: в ключевых словах ли, либо в чём, потому что я убеждена, что таких ресурсов, таких фотографий очень и очень много.

Я понял так: проблема, скорее всего, не в том, что таких работ мало, а в том, что мы слишком долго искали **архивы/ресурсы с правильным названием**, вместо того чтобы искать **реальные поверхности публикации**, где это живёт. И да, white list я бы не выключал совсем, а **оставил только как taste-anchor**, не как target-resource.

У меня сейчас ощущение, что стопор в двух местах:

- мы слишком узко держали класс источников: искали “сайты-архивы”, а твой объект может массово жить в `marketplace card studios`, `Instagram accounts`, `product-promo agencies`, `Asian KV / commercial poster ecosystems`, `portfolio/account clusters`;
- мы слишком привязывались к словам вроде `poster / campaign / key visual`, а у тебя объект шире: если это **стильная product/static card с интегрированным текстом**, она уже валидна, даже если это не “постер” в чистом виде.

Три вопроса, которые реально меняют поиск:

1. Правильно ли я теперь фиксирую объект так:
   **любой коммерческий static**, где `product/object + integrated type` сделаны стильно и современно,
   и сюда **входят** marketplace cards, promo statics, social statics, e-commerce hero visuals, launch cards, Instagram promos?

2. Правильно ли я понимаю, что теперь `target-resource` — это не обязательно “сайт-архив”, а вообще **любая repeatable surface**:
   аккаунт, студия, агентство, раздел сайта, marketplace-card publisher, Instagram page, Asian visual platform page — лишь бы там было много on-brief работ?

3. Что для тебя важнее на следующем заходе:
   - найти **где это публикуется массово**;
   - или найти **какие слова реально открывают этот пласт**, включая marketplace / e-commerce / promo language?

Если ответишь коротко на эти 3 пункта, я уже не буду снова уводить в “кейсики и архивчики”, а зафиксирую правильную ветку.
